items.summary: “Technologies that help the utility be more efficient in terms of building infrastructure … is a space that we're looking at,” Exelon’s Climate Change Investment Initiative lead told ESG Dive.

items.title: How Low Can PG&E Stock Go When The Risk Is Its Own?
items.summary: PG&E (PCG) trades at about $12.94, the bottom of its 52-week range and about 32% below its high. Over the past twelve months it lost 12.2% while the S&P 500 gained 18.5%. That gap did not come from a market crash. And in market shocks since 2007, its deepest fall includes a one-day break in PG&E's own price data.

items.title: Exelon (EXC), Why Is The Utility Getting Fresh Attention?
items.summary: Exelon (EXC) has drawn fresh attention after recent trading, with the share price closing at US$42.07. Investors now have a clearer snapshot of how this regulated utility group currently trades. Recent trading has been softer, with the share price return declining 1.34% over the last session and falling 8.42% over 90 days. Exelon’s 5 year total shareholder return of 43.13% reflects a steadier long run compounding story despite that weaker near term momentum. Compare Exelon’s recent pullback...

items.title: Exxon’s 11 Million-Gallon Refinery Goes Dark. How High Can Midwest Gas Prices Go?
items.summary: A flooded pump has knocked one of the Midwest's biggest refineries offline at the worst possible moment, and fuel markets from Chicago to Pittsburgh are already stretched thin. The question now is how long Exxon can stay dark before prices in the region hit a new breaking point.

items.title: Alphabet, Exelon, and Patterson-UTI Just Paid Shareholders. Here’s What They Got.
items.summary: Three companies with nothing in common all sent checks to shareholders within the same two-day window, and the reasons behind each payment reveal something very different about where each business is headed.

items.title: Is PG&E Stock Cheap, Or Just Waiting On California?
items.summary: PG&E (PCG) has lost about 13% over the past twelve months while the S&P 500 gained 17%. The California utility now trades at 9.5 times earnings against an S&P 500 median of 22.9, the kind of gap value buyers hunt for. So what has the market marked down: the utility, or the state it operates in.

items.title: How Is Exelon’s Stock Performance Compared to Other Regulated Utilities Stocks
items.summary: Exelon has underperformed its industry peers over the past year, as analysts remain neutral on the company’s future outlook.
